etymologies.etymologyHTML: Via French format and German Format, from New Latin liber fōrmātus (“book fashioned”), from fōrmō (“I shape, fashion”).

definitions.definition: The layout of a publication or document.

quote.citation: 1896, George Haven Putnam, Books and Their Makers During the Middle Ages:
quote.text: The older manuscripts had been written in a much larger format than that found convenient for university work.

definitions.definition: (by extension) The form of presentation of something.
(radio) The type of programming that a radio station broadcasts; such as a certain genre of music, news, sports, talk, etc.
To create or edit the layout of a document.
Change a document so it will fit onto a different type of page.
(computing) To prepare a mass storage medium for initial use, erasing any existing data in the process.
